Possibly due to the increased sunlight it receives growing above the clouds, heavens lemons lack the acidity of normal sun lemons.

Though it resembles a tree, cloud bananas actually grow from an oversized herb. That does not, however, make them any less sweet.

17559.description: Infusions made with this hardy brown-black foliage are believed to restore vigor.

17560.description: A small bead of naturally formed glass that could pass off as an eye, if viewed from thirty paces...in the fog.

Lower aetherial conductivity than regular mythril makes this a poor substitute for the precious green metal...unless low aetherial conductivity is what you require.

Not technically as light as an actual feather, this rare variety of iron weighs slightly less than normal iron, making it a preferable alternative...if enough can be procured.

19850.description: A nutty grain that can be substituted for flour in breads and noodles. Found across the Three Great Continents, but grown in abundance in the heart of Gyr Abania.

19851.description:
A sweet yet slightly tangy fruit with a thin skin and a fleshy orange interior. Can be found in the warmer valleys of Gyr Abania.

A greenish pink plum common across the eastern continent of Othard.

**EXP Bonus:** +3% **Duration:** 30m

19853.description: The root of the quick-growing kudzu vine is dug up and processed into kudzu powder which serves as a substitute for animal-based gelatins in Far Eastern desserts. It also is believed to exhibit healing properties, and can be found in most Hingan and Doman apothecaries.

19854.description: While just as brilliantly purple, this Far Eastern cousin of the wizard eggplant is noticeably thinner, and thus requires less time to cook.

19855.description: The spicy daikon radishes of Othard are known to grow as long and thick as a grown Hyur's forearm.

19856.description: These tubers can be several times sweeter than most fruit, and as such are commonly processed into sugar for sweetening cakes and other confections.

19857.description: Jhammel ginger's bulbous, aromatic roots can be sliced fresh and added to stews and seafood dishes to remove gaminess, ground and steeped in hot water to cure head colds, or dried and ground into a powder to use as a spice for breads and cookies.

19858.description: Gyr Abanian carrots are not only longer, but a far deeper orange─nay, crimson─than those grown in central and western Eorzea.

19859.description: Similar to green onions in flavor, the leeks of Gyr Abania are several times thicker, and far more piquant.

19860.description: If removed from the ground when less than a fulm in length, bamboo shoots can be peeled and the fleshy interior eaten. A popular ingredient in Far Eastern stews and stir-fries.

19861.description: Crisp mountain popotoes contain high quantities of starch that create a viscous paste when the tubers are ground. This paste can be eaten raw, fried into cakes, or added to stews for thickening.

19862.description: These emerald legumes grow two to three beans per pod on stout bushes that are ready for harvest in the early fall. The beans are most often pressed into the milk which is used to make tofu, or fermented into various savory pastes and sauces.

19863.description: These fungi native to the Far East are rarely eaten raw, the majority of those harvested dried, then used to make soup stock.

19864.description: A pungent spice that can be used in seed form, or ground into a powder, enhancing the aroma tenfold.

19865.description: Though they appear solid from the outside, the cylindrical root nodules of the lotus flower are riddled with holes, possibly to accommodate for the waterlogged environments in which the plant grows.

19866.description: The sweet, tightly packed leaves of Othardian sun cabbages are deceptively sweet, making them perfect in salads or stews.

19867.description: With an aroma similar to licorice, both the stalks and the seeds of this Othardian herb can be used to enhance the flavor of exotic Far Eastern dishes.

19868.description: A close cousin to highland wheat, Gyr Abanian wheat has been improved by Ala Mhigan farmers over generations to increase both flavor and yield.

19869.description:
A hard, orange fruit common in eastern Othard. It is well known that seven summers must pass before a newly planted persimmon tree will bear fruit.

**EXP Bonus:** +3% **Duration:** 30m
(Duration can be extended to 60m by consuming multiple servings)

19870.description: While not edible, the leaves of the persimmon tree are oft used in the preservation of other food.

19872.description: Clear, odorless water taken from one of the many springs found on Othard's Fanged Crescent.

19879.description: This edible seaweed can be consumed raw, or dried into paper-like squares and wrapped around sticky rice.

19880.description: A distant cousin of malm kelp, Ruby Tide kelp is harvested and dried in the sun to enhance flavor. Squares of the seaweed are cut and steeped in boiling water to create one of the savory broths used in Hingan cuisine.

19881.description: A variety of algae found in the Ruby Sea, commonly harvested for its salt.

24570.description: A collection of items that look suitable for use in creating furnishings, and aren't *that* dirty.

27753.description: The brilliantly white flower of an unusual variety of cotton plant.

27759.description: Flowers of the coincidentally short-stalked dwarven cotton plant are used by the people bearing the same name to create everything from undergarments to beards.

27761.description: As difficult to lay hands upon as bubbles on the water, from these cocoons can be spun a rare type of silk.

27776.description: Naturally sparkling water bottled at the source. Do not shake before opening.

27779.description: This plant that blooms with myriad tiny flowers smelling of honey.

27785.description: A type of gerbera named for its bright white flowers.

27803.description: Volcanic ash compacted by pressure and time into firm stone.

27805.description: As the name suggests, this variety of stone is more strongly aspected than typical wind rock.

27806.description: A deceptively plain stone that, when cracked, momentarily erupts with bright light.

27807.description: Several small pieces of dark unpolished quartz.

27809.description: A herb cultivated for both its medicinal uses and pleasant fragrance.

27810.description: The azure flowers of this plant brighten the landscape when in bloom, but its true value is in its leaves.

27816.description: The thick branch of a white oak tree.

27817.description: A more colorful version of the typically white mineral used by leatherworkers to tan animal hides.

27818.description: A dark purple root vegetable with a reddish stalk, differing somewhat in vitamin content from the orange carrot.

27819.description: A particularly fragrant variety of apricot.

27820.description: This olive cultivar can be used to produce a large amount of high-quality cooking oil.

27821.description: This sweet spice made from the dried floral buds is used both as flavoring and in essential oils.

27822.description: An easy-to-peel variety of popoto with thin skin and a high starch content.

27823.description: This fancifully frilly parsley has an unobtrusive flavor that makes it perfect for use in otherwise bland dishes or as a garnish.

27824.description: This common root vegetable doubles as a source of inexpensive sugar.

27825.description: The slight acidity of this bright tomato is guaranteed to whet one's appetite, making it a long-standing favorite of tavern owners throughout Norvrandt.

27826.description: The flavor of these cultivated grapes has been intensified using a special bacteria. Though unpleasant to eat whole, they are suitable for juicing and fermentation.

27827.description: A dark aromatic spice used in cooking as well as pickling.

27829.description: A bulbous white mushroom that grows wild in forests.

27830.description: This short-grain rice is more absorbent than other varieties and does not clump together when cooked.

27831.description: A powerfully sweet variety of apple.

27832.description: This staple grain was grown at high elevation.

27833.description: These large, spring green beans are easy to cultivate, and have served as a staple food for millennia.

27834.description: A normal-sized piece of a massive hive created by a giant honey bee swarm.

27835.description: A tiny lemon replete with sour juice.

27836.description: This refreshing herb is suitable for use in cooking, essential oils, and tea.

27837.description: Beans that, with some effort, will become grounds suitable for brewing fragrant coffee.

27954.description: A translucent crystalline substance often used in making glass, firesand, and dyes.

27968.description: Mineral-rich water bottled at its high-elevation source.

28199.description: Once the dense coal has been ground into powder and mixed with water, it can be used as a substitute for ink. Be sure to keep it away from white clothing, as the stains are a bugger to get out.

28200.description: This selection of rare varieties of salt and spices native to Amh Araeng can be used to add a dash of elegance and a pinch of class to even the most unappetizing of dishes.

28201.description: Every region of Norvrandt is, for some reason, blessed with an astonishing variety of glittering, shimmering, sparkling, and otherwise shiny stones. Il Mheg is no exception, as is amply demonstrated by these fine specimens.

28202.description: In the hands of an artisan, these bits and pieces gathered from around Amh Araeng will eventually become the decorations used to adorn Eulmore's fleet of airships. In fact, it took another sort of artisan to even find them in the first place, having been forced to separate the proverbial wheat from the chaff in some of the desert's most perilous locations.

28203.description: While not everything included in this assortment of locally sourced materials could be considered valuable, the various items combine to convey the very essence of Kholusia. This could, however, be attributed to the pungent oceanic odor they all seem to share.

28716.description: A partially congealed ball of sticky sap extracted from a sandalwood tree.

28717.description: A decent-sized piece of rock containing the precious metal beryllium.

28765.description: The distinct lack of trees is one of many problems the first people to settle in Ishgard chose to ignore, making this otherwise commonplace material─sourced from the East Shroud─extremely valuable.

28766.description: While this may look much like any other iron ore found in middle La Noscea, there are subtle differences that only an expert in the field will recognize. The name, for one, is considerably longer.

28767.description: This sand gathered in central Thanalan is not only fine, but extremely well-behaved, choosing to stay in one closely knit lump while jostling alongside the rest of your possessions.

28768.description: Though this hardy plant can grow almost anywhere, the snow-blasted precipices of Ishgard have so far proven too steep a challenge for it to overcome. This particular specimen was harvested in lower La Noscea, an environment far more conducive to plant life─or any sort of life, for that matter.

28769.description: Ash! A-Ah! Savior of the Firmament!♪

28770.description: Although upper La Noscea seems rather a distant location from which to source something as simple as salt, the Ishgardians are nothing if not particular in their tastes.

28771.description: The electrum ore found in upper La Noscea is believed to be far better suited to the skybuilders' needs than any other variety. Were anyone to ask them why, they would, in most cases be met with a response along the line of, “Because it just is.”

28772.description: The tradition of measuring powdered substances in units of “pinches” has been the cause of many arguments, largely due to differences in finger size between the various races. Folk in eastern Thanalan, where this sample was gathered, have been known to ask Lalafells to measure when selling, and Roegadyn when buying, for obvious reasons.

28773.description: It is a well known fact among botanists that the flax in the South Shroud is superior to every other kind, for reasons far too complicated and boring for anyone else to care about.

28774.description: Having only traveled the relatively short distance from the Coerthas central highlands to Ishgard, this spring water is still remarkably fresh, though the icy chill threatens to freeze it inside the bottle.

28775.description: Few members of the mortal races are equipped to make the perilous journey to the Churning Mists, and those who do normally hope to have more than a log or two to show for their troubles.

28776.description: Why the skybuilders would specify that their straw be brought from the Dravanian forelands is anyone's guess. Perhaps the smell helps their chocobos sleep more peacefully?

28777.description: The time spent mining this ore in the Dravanian hinterlands would perhaps have seemed less arduous if you had the faintest idea how the skybuilders plan to use it.

28778.description: You have a sneaking suspicion that you may have lost some of the sand during the return journey from the Sea of Clouds, though the amount you have in your possession should still suffice.

28779.description: The thought of happy skybuilders drinking delicious tea was the only motivation you needed as you risked life and limb gathering these leaves in the Sea of Clouds.

28780.description: There are easier places to collect spring water than the Dravanian forelands, though it seems your personal safety is not especially high on the skybuilders' list of concerns.

28781.description: Compared to most places in Gyr Abania, the Peaks has more than its fair share of trees, so who would object to you taking a few logs? Bloodthirsty Qiqirn and rampaging ruud suuds, that's who. Or perhaps they just see you as an easy meal?

28782.description: The Ruby Sea is not especially well known as a prime location for mining, though those who are nautically minded can uncover all sorts of rare and unique treasures. Whether the skybuilders choose to turn this into fine jewelry or something more mundane, like a tea strainer, remains to be seen.

28783.description: Venomous snakes are something of a rarity in Ishgard, so the skybuilders have ordered that some be delivered from the Azim Steppe to help improve morale. Workers displaying a lack of enthusiasm will be given some time in “the pit” to rediscover their commitment to the cause.

28784.description: While the Lochs are better known as a source of salt, the rich veins of ore are drawing in miners from far and wide.

28785.description: Yanxia is rich in both flora and fauna, and horsetail forms a major part of the diet of many grazing creatures.

28786.description: When an Ishgardian culinarian stated that her latest dish needed a pinch of salt, the skybuilders sought out the very best, though perhaps more than a single pinch would be required to make the lengthy journey to the Lochs worthwhile.

28787.description: While water from the Ruby Sea may not sound particularly appealing, this was actually brought from a small freshwater spring on one of the surrounding islands. Drinking this is unlikely to result in life-threatening dehydration.

28788.description: A pinch of anything tends not to be an awful lot, though this particular sand from the Azim Steppe is apparently worth more than its weight in gold.

28789.description: Quite why a particular type of vine that can only be found in the Azim Steppe is necessary to the skybuilders' plans has yet to be explained. Perhaps they are planning to surprise you with a work of surpassing genius? Or perhaps not.

28790.description: Obviously, none of the skybuilders has even heard of the Rak'tika Greatwood, though the specific qualities they seek in their timber can most easily be found in the white ash trees that grow there.

28791.description: If a porous rock from the bottom of the ocean is required in the rebuilding of Ishgard, then so be it. Your job is to mine, not question the reasoning behind such dubious demands.

28792.description: Why submit a boring chunk of gold ore when you can bring one all the way from Il Mheg instead?

28793.description: This cotton must be very special indeed for you to bring it all the way from Lakeland in the First. You can only hope that the skybuilders appreciate you going the extra malm. And traveling to another world.

28794.description: One day, this poor lizard is chasing other, smaller scurrying creatures across the desert plains of Amh Araeng, and the next, it is being transported to another world and dragged lashing and kicking to Ishgard. The chances of the cold-blooded scalekin being content in its frozen new surroundings are slim at best, and you can only hope that the skybuilders are grateful to you for supplying a miserable and motionless lizard.

28795.description: Were the other contributors to hear that you traveled to Amh Araeng in the First simply to procure wheat, they would think you are just trying to show off.

28796.description: The isle of Kholusia is known by the inhabitants of Norvrandt to have the very finest of gold sand. Whether this is up to the impossibly high standards of the skybuilders will only become apparent when it is submitted for inspection.

28797.description: Any water gathered from Il Mheg is likely to have been enchanted by either the pixies or the Fuath, though that is a problem for the skybuilders, not you, to worry about.

28798.description: Thankfully, the resin appears to have suffered no ill effects during your return from the Rak'tika Greatwood, meaning that it is still a gelatinous blob with seemingly no practical application whatsoever.

28909.description: While there seems to be an endless supply of these in Yanxia, why anyone would actually want them is unclear. They have a taste to match their appearance, in other words, revolting.

28910.description: The ocean depths are dark and full of horrors... But also, rather a good location to harvest salt. Just watch out for the horrors.

28916.description: What is worse than being born a toad? Being born a toad and then carried against your wishes from your home in western Thanalan to icy Ishgard, where if you don't freeze to death, are likely to be chopped up and boiled in a pot. That is what is worse. Much worse, in fact.

29669.description: It is a relatively simple matter for a skilled botanist to collect latex from a specified plant in a specified vessel by specified means. Excruciating, yes, but simple.

29674.description: A hunk of fossilized resin of *very* particular hue, clarity, and age.

29676.description: Darker (and more specific) than your average matter.

29894.description:
A sharp rap across the back of the thigh in the cold, crisp Ishgardian morning air with one of these light and flexible branches is a surefire way to blow away the proverbial cobwebs of any workers caught yawning.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29895.description:
One can only hope that whatever purpose the skybuilders have in mind for this hardy plant was worth depriving some herbivorous creature of its leafy goodness.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29896.description:
Something of a mixed bag of metallic elements, but as everyone knows, smithies love a good surprise. Just not when they're swinging a hammer dangerously close to their fingers.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29897.description:
A special place in one of the seven hells exists for those who attempt to fob off the skybuilders by mixing in regular sand with the copper, or so the skybuilders would have one believe.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

29898.description:
The sap slowly leaking from the logs tends to attract ants, which even the skybuilders have yet to find a use for. This may come as a surprise considering the plethora of bizarre items they request, and it may only be a matter of time until some bright spark invents ant sandwiches.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29899.description:
Any insect foolhardy enough to attempt sampling its delight will invariably find itself trapped within this glutinous substance, preserved for future generations to study and possibly experiment on. Still, there are worse ways to go than being enveloped in one's favorite sweet treat.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29900.description:
Included in a surprising number of recipes and concoctions despite its only notable property being “it smells nice.”

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29901.description:
Zinc is said to prevent a number of common ailments. However, it must be noted that attempting to ingest it in its current state may actually *cause* problems such as broken teeth and stomachache, usually in that order.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29902.description:
There are few dishes that cannot be improved with a sprinkling of salt. Strangely, this even includes a number of desserts, which flies in the face of all common logic.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29903.description:
In the event that one somehow accidentally mixes this with normal sand, the two can be separated by waving a magnet nearby. This knowledge may─or more likely, may not─save your life one day.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

29904.description:
Although such logs are the perfect material for fashioning rafts and canoes, the distinctly frozen bodies of water that surround Ishgard scupper the locals' chances of enjoying the pleasures of boating.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29905.description:
Any ancient myths describing darts made from a sprig of mistletoe neglect to mention the fact that when thrown, it displays the airborne grace of a drunken, one-winged chicken.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29906.description:
A bee colony will often respond to the presence of intruders by swarming their intended target and using their own body heat to cook it alive. The skybuilders have discovered that this can be utilized to keep their hands warm, although the fact that said bees are still very much capable of stinging does present a minor flaw in this otherwise brilliant idea.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29907.description:
In some parts of Eorzea, straw is used to weave hats with wide peaks to keep the sun from the wearer's eyes. Fortunately─or perhaps unfortunately─for Ishgardians, there is seldom enough sunlight to warrant such headwear, and the vicious winds would prevent the owner from remaining behatted for more than a few scant moments.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29908.description:
For Ishgardians, discussing the virtues of various blends of tea is almost as much of a pastime as actually drinking the stuff. This fine selection of choice leaves could be placed in the center of a table to serve to facilitate stimulating conversation, while the skybuilders continue to labor away in the bitter cold outside.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29909.description:
A lot less blue than one might expect, although it tastes about right.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29910.description:
While some of the skybuilders were in favor of naming this substance “purple stuff,” the need to follow a more sensible naming convention eventually prevailed.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29911.description:
Plans to use this sticky, black substance to cover the streets of Ishgard were vehemently opposed, as it would ruin the uniformly grey aesthetic─which on most days includes the sky itself.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29912.description:
The bright hue of this valuable substance does make it stand out from the surrounding rocks and so forth, but only under the condition that one is able to find the damnable stuff in the first place.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29913.description:
“Mica” would make rather a nice name for a person, if it were not already taken by this rather unremarkable rock.

Used in level 60 crafting recipes.

29914.description:
The tiny acorn that grew into this mighty oak had its life cut tragically short by the cruel axe of a woodsman (or possibly woodslady). If there is any justice in the world, it will be born anew as a nice dresser or an attractive hat stand.

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29915.description:
While even Ishgard's finest ornithologist would be hard-pressed to identify the bird from which this came, one thing is certain: there are more where this came from, unless said bird only ever possessed a single feather.

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29916.description:
Careless owners of high-walled castles in faerie tales often allow these to grow over said walls, thereby allowing dashing heroes to infiltrate the premises to steal jewels, damsels in distress, scones from the pantry, and so forth.

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29917.description:
One skybuilder was heard to claim that to assign grades to living creatures is degrading. The response was, “No, taking the grade away from it would be called degrading.”

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29918.description:
According to local legend, a night raid on a Temple Knights encampment was foiled when the assailants wandered into a patch of barbgrass. Nothing gives the game away quite like pained squeals of, “Oh, my poor bottom!”

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29919.description:
Due to the fact it is almost identical in appearance to mythril ore, it is sometimes known as “fool's mythril.” Conversely, actual mythril is often referred to as “fool's mythrite.”

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29920.description:
Despite the potentially misleading name, it can also be collected in summer and autumn. Winter, however, is generally out of the question, for obvious reasons.

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29921.description:
Were the skybuilders less exacting in their demands, the standard alumen found in market stalls across Eorzea would be more than sufficient. Many volunteers suspect that such tasks are set merely to test their patience.

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29922.description:
If you think this rock is uninteresting, you should see the grade 1 skybuilders' rock, which is so plain that it can blend into any background by virtue of its sheer dullness.

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29923.description:
The name makes it sound far more sinister than it actually is.

Used in level 70 crafting recipes.

29924.description:
Think of all the walnuts that could have grown on this tree had it not been cut down! Walnuts for breakfast, walnuts for elevenses, walnuts for luncheon... The possibilities were endless.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29925.description:
Resin this pure, this beautiful is far too good for the skybuilders. Perhaps you should keep it all to yourself. They need never know.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29926.description:
There is a possibility that some grade 1 wheat slipped in by mistake.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29927.description:
One of the skybuilder's children asked, “Is this what sheep are made from?” The answer was a resounding, “I'm not sure. Possibly.”

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29928.description:
Venomous, but not fatally so. Perfect for practical jokes and party tricks.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29929.description:
Has the potential to be made into something very scary indeed, like spiked pauldrons or an enormous battleaxe. In all likelihood, however, it will probably become a slightly extravagant kettle or decorative letter opener.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29930.description:
With a name that long, one might be forgiven for expecting it to be some sort of miraculous super-salt, capable of turning even the blandest dish into a festival of flavor. Sadly, this is not the case, although it is nonetheless rather good as far as salt goes.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29931.description:
Most people realize “cloud drop” is just a fancy way to say “rain.” Not many customers would be willing to pay for mere rainwater, but cloud drop water, on the other hand...

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29932.description:
Said to be blessed by cloud spirits, which may or may not be a good thing. Still, “blessed” is infinitely preferable to “cursed.”

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29933.description:
Basalt actually has very little in common with salt, despite its name being approximately two-thirds the same.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

29934.description:
As the skybuilders prefer to use wooden planks of standardized dimensions, this log is already cut to be exactly the length they require, to minimize the carpenters' workload. One can only hope they appreciate the extra effort by throwing a few more scrips your way.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29935.description:
Although the practical applications of a piece of hardened sap are somewhat unclear, it is at least considerably less sticky than unhardened sap, which helps to keep it free of impurities such as loose hairs, bits of pocket fluff, and so on.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29936.description:
What about this wheat makes it artisanal? Those in the know claim it is massaged daily and fed beer, which is the reason for the delicious marbled texture. Or perhaps they were talking about some sort of cow?

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29937.description:
To the untrained eye, this may appear to be no different from any other cotton boll. Those with *trained* eyes, however, will notice that it is pink, not the usual white.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29938.description:
Those wondering what separates this from a non-artisanal dawn lizard need only observe the way it devours its prey. For a carnivorous, slavering scalekin, it has the most impeccable table manners, or more precisely, “blood-spattered patch of ground manners.”

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29939.description:
Believed to be a piece of fossilized cloud.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29940.description:
It seems there are almost as many varieties of rock salt as there are varieties of rock, if the skybuilders' somewhat arbitrary system of assigning names is to be believed.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29941.description:
Rather than simply being free of impurities, this water actually possesses the ability to preemptively destroy any impurities that dare to come near it. As such, only those pure of heart can drink of it without being killed instantly, or so it is rumored.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29942.description:
One of the few substances known to be both edible and highly explosive. While some spicy ingredients are said to be capable of blowing one's head off, in this case, it is no exaggeration.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29943.description:
In the Brume, to be “jaded” means to have a large piece of jade thrown at the back of one's head. Thankfully, the prohibitive pricing of this precious substance means that such incidents are rare.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

29968.description: Seasoned miners will recognize this as a type of sulfide, its composition lending its surface a permanent sheen that makes it look like a glowing ember in the light.

29970.description: A shiny piece of Purpure carapace.

29972.description: A rough-cut log of merbau timber, bearing the wood's distinctive scent.

29974.description: A flowering plant with tiny purple blooms.

29978.description: Presumably named by one of history's many oppressed lower classes, this fern's appellation cannot but refer to the pretentious way in which it curls.

30485.description: A small variety of dill characterized by its sweet fragrance. Finds use in both medicinal and culinary applications.

30486.description: A decent-sized piece of rock rich in a highly durable, naturally occurring alloy.

30498.description: An assortment of materials that, when assembled properly, can make a gathering tool that even dragons can use.

30499.description: An assortment of materials that, when assembled properly, can make a tool that even dragons can use to weave.

30500.description: An assortment of materials that, when assembled properly, can make a crafting tool that even dragons can use.

30501.description: An assortment of materials that, when cooked by the right culinarian, can make a feast even the most ancient of beings can enjoy.

30502.description: An assortment of materials that can be used to print a book. Instructions not included.

30591.description: An uncut stone imbued with so much aetheric lightning energy as to echo with tiny claps of thunder.

30592.description: The pink leaves of this peculiar mint thrum gently with lightning energy.

31125.description: Oddly enough, all of the specific requirements relate to the wood's aroma, which is strange considering it will most likely be covered in several layers of varnish, thereby obfuscating the original scent.

31127.description: Schorl is already in and of itself rather a specific thing to request, and it is somewhat surprising to find that it would play a significant part in improving an artisan's tool of the trade.

31130.description: The last remains of a great arboreal pillar, as old as time, that once towered over the earliest forms of life at the world's beginning. Smells a bit funny.

31132.description: Even among its rocky brethren, this specimen is especially ancient, having weathered the passing of ages, and is regarded as the grandfather of all stones. Well, not literally, that would be impossible for reasons far too complex to explain here. Or anywhere, for that matter.

31276.description:
Makes a satisfying “thwack” sound when swung through the air. On the other hand, attempting to actually hit something will cause it to break immediately, so it is reserved only for scare tactics.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31277.description:
Compared to the grade 2 variety, this is the good shite.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31278.description:
The first miner to discover this particular variety described it as “extra-ore-dinary” and was met with a chorus of groans from her peers.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31279.description:
Some might argue that it would be easier to locate a living bomb and wait for it to explode than to scrabble about in the dirt and undergrowth looking for particles of ash from one that had exploded previously. The problem lies in finding volunteers who are not only foolhardy enough to attempt it, but hardy enough to survive.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

31280.description:
Care must be taken when working with ebony wood, as its sawdust is both highly flammable and toxic. Strangely, the skybuilders failed to mention this...

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31281.description:
Sesame is not only a useful plant, but the mere mention of its name is believed to open many doors in a very literal sense.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31282.description:
Often misheard as “cotton bowl,” which has led to several nigh on useless pieces of fluffy tableware being submitted to the skybuilders.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31283.description:
Unlike some other ores requested by the skybuilders, they actually deigned to give the name of the type of metal they would like in this case, rather than simply “some ore.”

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31284.description:
This particular type of salt is for sprinkling on rocks to make them taste better, hence the name “rock salt.”

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31285.description:
Hardsilver's inherent hardness is somewhat difficult to gauge in granular form.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

31286.description: The aesthetically pleasing bark of this particular tree allows it to be used in its natural state to give a rustic feel to a home's interior. On the other hand, “rustic” is often used to mean “we can save time and effort by convincing gullible customers that having bits of rough-cut wood all over the place is somehow desirable.”

31287.description: Used in a variety of medical treatments despite being highly toxic. Failure to adhere to the correct dosage may lead to symptoms far worse than the ailment it was meant to cure.

31288.description: One of the skybuilders has been tasked with kissing every toad they receive on the off chance of it being a cursed prince. This, however, is suspected to be one of the many tasks designed to keep troublesome workers out of mischief, along with polishing the coal and washing the soap.

31289.description: A naturally occurring substitute for rope, perfect for swinging through the trees while yodeling like a buffoon.

31290.description: This variety is often used in tea leaf reading, and is said to result in a high rate of good fortunes, though most tasseomancers base their readings more on what they think the customer wants to hear than the patterns left in the cup.

31291.description: Though similar substances exist in other regions, the Diadem variety tends to be more highly coveted. This may simply be due to its scarcity rather than any intrinsic properties, as by and large, the more difficult something is to obtain, the more people want it.

31292.description: In recent years, there have been calls to abandon the use of “pinches” as a unit of measurement for powders. However, the fact that an amount equal to a single pinch is rarely enough to cause even the most sensitive of scales to budge leads to difficulties when deciding on a weight-based standard.

31293.description: The name may indicate that there are very specific criteria to pass muster with the skybuilders, but the taste and smell are the same as almost any other type of water. That is to say: it tastes of nothing and smells of nothing.

31294.description: As is often the case with items found in the Diadem, this iron sand possesses unique properties. It is magnetically attracted not only to metallic objects, but a range of organic materials, such as skin and clothing, which means it is often gathered regardless of one's intentions.

31295.description: This flaky, lightweight stone is a firm favorite with street performers who demonstrate their strength by smashing through rock with their bare hands.

31296.description:
Due to cedar being a natural repellent for moths─which can be both extremely large and ferocious in some parts─many adventurers have taken to carrying it about their person. Hefting around an entire log might be going a touch overboard, however.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31297.description:
“He tried to take it from me, or at least, he looked like he wanted to. So I cut him. Can't blame a man for keeping his resin to himself, can you?”
─Excerpt from *How to Win Friends and Execute People: Climbing the Ranks of the Temple Knights*
by unknown author

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31298.description:
May contain traces of chaff.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31299.description:
In this case, the word “gossamer” is applied in a literal sense, as each boll is covered in a fine layer of cobweb. This is kept intact until the cotton is spun into thread, which grants it extraordinary resilience to wear and tear.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31300.description:
As one can imagine, there is a host of practical applications for a venomous snake in the Ishgardian reconstruction efforts. These include the production of snake wine, in which the scalekin is preserved in alcohol that gains a unique flavor and medicinal properties. In several cases, the snake has been known to spring to life after moons of being entirely submerged in the liquid.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31301.description:
“Kingly” is not an adjective that is often applied to metals of any sort, though in the case of aurum regis, it seems perfectly fitting, for some reason.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31302.description:
Many people prefer to keep such chunks whole so that they may be used as “salt rocks.” These are placed in the center of the dining table so that anyone who feels their meal is lacking in saltiness can simply lick it and carry on with their meal.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31303.description:
Often confused with falsespring water, which is remarkably similar apart from the fact it smells like a wet dog.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31304.description:
“Despite the creature having been dead for millennia, fossilized, and then ground to dust, I was able to extrapolate its diet, breeding habits, and susceptibility to hiccups from the single, remaining fragment of vertebrae.”
─Excerpt from *On the Trail of the Thunder Lizards*

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31305.description:
Mudstone may not be the most impressive of substances, but becoming a solid piece of rock after an extended period as a sticky semiliquid is something of an improvement.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

31306.description:
Grade 3 and artisanal it may be, yet the name of the tree from which it came is an enigma enveloped in a mystery. Before the skybuilders and their bizarre naming conventions, it was simply...log.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31307.description:
The grade is determined by the number of vilekin encased within each piece. Fewer is generally considered to be better, unless the buyer happens to be a naturalist, in which case, the opposite is true. They have been known to pay absurd amounts for the most heavily infested specimens.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31308.description:
These bolls contain roughly twice the amount of cotton as the regular sort, but due to the thickness of the plant's stems, take roughly twice as much effort to harvest.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31309.description:
Rice remains something of a novelty in Ishgard, though the skybuilders seem to be experts on the subject regardless. Apparently, they can tell the difference between the truly artisanal and the merely humdrum.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31310.description:
The artisanal vines that are chosen for the Firmament tend to stand out from the common-or-garden varieties. One could say they are vine for attention.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31311.description:
One of the few stones light enough to float in water.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31312.description:
Most recipients of such eggs would prefer them without a tiny, carnivorous scalekin inside.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31313.description:
Though alumen is commonly used in the tanning of animal hide, the artisanal can supposedly be used to tan other materials, such as hair or soil. Such claims have yet to be verified, however.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31314.description:
Many apprentice potters have been known to misinterpret the meaning of “throwing a pot,” leading to hilarious capers, instant dismissal, or both.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31315.description:
Granite is said to be phaneritic, or in layman's terms, macroscopically crystalline.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

31766.description: For all the feathers adorning a cloudkin's body, only a rare few could be considered oddly delicate. Those are generally found around the wingpit, the avian equivalent of an armpit, obviously.

31767.description: Oddly delicate for a birch log, though still fairly hefty by most people's standards.

31768.description: Adamantite, as the name would suggest, is anything but delicate, though this particular sample is perhaps ever-so-slightly less than “practically indestructible.”

31769.description: Hopefully not so delicate that it will shatter into a thousand pieces at the first attempt to refine it.

32005.description:
As many Ishgardian schoolchildren will attest, telling one's detractors “Sticks and stones may break my bones, but words shall never harm me” is an open invitation to be assaulted with said objects.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

32006.description:
Since time immemorial, this robust plant has helped many a convicted criminal dance the hempen jig.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

32007.description:
Any smith worth their salt will have a vast amount of ores, ingots, rivets, rings, and plates at their disposal, although finding space to store it all can prove most bothersome. Some have even taken to employing retainers for the sole purpose of lugging their surplus junk around.

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

32008.description:
Primarily used as a vital component in a children's toy whereby hair and a beard may be applied to a picture of a man's face by means of an ingenious magnetic wand. (For ages three and up.)

Used in level 20 crafting recipes.

32009.description:
Used in the construction of various musical instruments and believed to imbue the music with a certain ethereal quality. This may or may not be due to the souls of elementals trapped within the wood, which brings a whole new meaning to the phrase “haunting melody.”

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32010.description:
The sesame plant is robust enough to grow in even the most inhospitable environments, including those in which the botanists tasked with gathering said plant are incapable of surviving. As valuable as sesame is, most would agree it is not worth risking life and limb for, not that the skybuilders seem particularly bothered by this when making their requests...

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32011.description:
A freshly picked cotton boll with the stem still attached is the perfect implement for cleaning one's ears, though it is likely that the skybuilders will notice if that same cotton boll is submitted to them after being used. They tend to object to that sort of thing.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32012.description:
Only a true skybuilder could look at a nondescript lump of grey, slightly metallic rock and say, “Yes, this is definitely grade 4 skybuilders' ore,” though it could be argued that this is because they are the ones who named it to begin with.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32013.description:
“But Mother, can we not break the salt rock into smaller chunks to save us all from having to lick the same piece? It seems awfully unhygienic.”
“No, my sweet prince, that would not be proper. Now lick the rock and put it back on the table.”
─Typical Ishgardian mealtime conversation

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32014.description:
A popular choice for hourglasses as the speed at which the sand falls is directly affected by how much those in close proximity are enjoying themselves. With a mythrite sand hourglass, time really does fly when one is having fun.

Used in level 40 crafting recipes.

32015.description:
Spruce is the wood of choice in all manner of carpentry projects, from enormous load-bearing beams to tiny intricately carved ornaments. So versatile is it that one wonders why the skybuilders even bother with the other types of timber.

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32016.description:
A prominent feature in many Starlight Celebration decorations, mistletoe is much loved by the people of Ishgard. Most people would probably view it rather differently, however, if they knew that the plant is in fact a voracious parasite that mercilessly drains the life from its host.

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32017.description:
You had best treat this warty little creature kindly as it may be a ninja's hellfrog in disguise. “Burned to death by flaming frog vomit” is hardly the sort of remark one wants in their obituary.

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32018.description:
Although such vines make perfectly adequate replacements for rope, it seems that the skybuilders have more than enough actual rope to make the use of this plant somewhat redundant.

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32019.description:
“There are few problems that cannot be resolved─or at least, forgotten about─over a nice cup of tea.”
─Ishgardian aphorism

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32020.description:
A naturally occurring alloy of gold and silver, though many would argue that it is worth less than the sum of its parts. Those expecting it to possess some sort of lightning-aspected aetherial properties due to the name are sure to be disappointed, although that has not prevented several unscrupulous merchants from advertising it as such.

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32021.description:
Another in a seemingly endless list of powdered substances that are of vital importance to alchemists, goldsmiths, and the like, but mean─to quote the common vernacular─bugger all to everyone else. Luckily, laymen need only know how much it will fetch at market and whether or not one must face any life-endangering peril to obtain it.

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32022.description:
A number of stringent tests are performed to determine the grade assigned to spring water, including the measurement of time taken to evaporate when poured into a shallow dish and placed next to a hot pig.

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32023.description:
Each grain of gold sand was once a whole nugget that has been gradually eroded over many thousands of years, which is a rather extreme example of depreciating value.

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32024.description:
Due to being formed from compressed layers of sediment, ragstone may contain rare and precious fossils. The skybuilders, however, care not a jot about any of that and will happily use it to whet their blades and so forth, much to the woe of naturalists throughout Eorzea.

Used in level 60 and 70 crafting recipes.

32025.description:
White cedar is known to be one of the most longevous species of tree, with one particular specimen estimated to be 1,852 years old, according to the number of growth rings. Of course, it probably would have lived a lot longer if not for a glory-seeking, axe-happy botanist.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32026.description:
Made from congealed primordial soup.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32027.description:
Ishgardian bakers organize a gathering known as a “wheat and greet,” in which they discuss a range of topics, such as the perfect method for wafting the smell of freshly baked bread into the streets to maximize profits.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32028.description:
When it comes to cotton bolls, this is the sovereign of softness, the commandant of comfort, the liege lord of loveliness.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32029.description:
Those who believe dogs are man's best friend have obviously never met a tortoise.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32030.description:
“The ambassador's receptions are noted in society for their host's exquisite taste that captivates his guests. The tray of gold nuggets his butlers pass around, however, often leads to confusion and broken teeth when said guests mistake them for chocolate treats.”
─*The Highs and Lows of Ishgardian High Society*

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32031.description:
This particular variety of rock salt has proved so popular with Ishgardian diners, that many choose to forgo their meal altogether and spend the evening licking the communal salt rock instead.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32032.description:
The advertising slogan, “Spring water never tasted so true,” has left many Ishgardians both impressed and baffled in equal measure. Merchants are hopeful that this will cause just the right amount of confusion to distract from the fact it is essentially identical to the grade 3 variety. And any other type of water, for that matter.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32033.description:
When the skybuilders were quizzed as to exactly what type of mineral comprises this sand, the reply was, “That information is on a need-to-know basis.” One would assume that those mining the stuff would need to know what they are supposed to be looking for, but the skybuilders move─and think─in mysterious ways.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32034.description:
Not only is this rock imbued with a spirit, but that spirit is feeling particularly blue. Perhaps being smashed repeatedly with a chisel will cheer it up.

Used in level 80 crafting recipes.

32035.description:
The word “log” fails to amply convey the undeniable majesty of this immaculate specimen. Unfortunately, there are no suitable substitutes, unless one is content to call it a “tree with all the sticky-outy bits cut off.”

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32036.description:
Being rather small, it is unusual for raspberries to be handled individually rather than by weight. This may also be because fruiterers are keen to avoid counting anything other than coins.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32037.description:
In this case, “artisanal” refers to the caiman itself rather than the person tasked with procuring it. This scalekin is particularly gifted in the art of nest building, or at least it was before being clobbered over the head and dragged off to the skybuilders.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32038.description:
As the skybuilders neglected to specify the exact type of cocoon they would like delivered, its contents remain unknown. It could be home to anything from a wamoura pupa to the larva of a parasitic wespe. Nothing good, in other words.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32039.description:
The countless tiny barbs at the tips of this hardy plant are believed to deter grazing beastkin. However, to counteract this, those creatures have developed an especially tough lining to the inside of their mouths, and could probably bite down on a handful of broken glass without so much as batting an eyelid.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32040.description:
According to certain scholars, the islands of the Sea of Clouds are kept suspended in the air by large amounts of cloudstone. It is therefore advised not to mine too much of this valuable resource as it may cause the island to plummet from the sky.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32041.description:
Spring water is said to result from a series of complex processes that unfold deep underground. But in a place like the Diadem, where the normal laws of nature appear to be ignored entirely, it is impossible to say exactly where this water comes from.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32042.description:
Be sure to hold this the right way up or it could be mistaken for a stalactite.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32043.description:
Similar─though rather less artisanal─sacks of silex are sold to the participants in Ul'dah's Coliseum. A well-aimed handful of the stuff can temporarily blind the opponent, though it is only a matter of time until these customers realize that the same is true of the sand that lines the arena floor, which is available for free.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32044.description:
Shines with all the colors of the rainbow, and even a few extra, like luminous black and fluorescent beige.

Used in expert crafting recipes.

32950.description: A rough-cut log of silver beech timber.

32951.description: A semi-translucent rock containing the rare mineral dolomite.

32952.description: A mysterious crystal of purest white.

32953.description: The cotton produced by this particular species is said to be as delicate to the touch as a raindrop. Unfortunately, this makes it rather difficult to pick without crushing the boll.

32954.description: Though this bark has a number of uses, being in an apparently semi-fossilized state does make it somewhat troublesome to work with.

32955.description: To the layman, hard water may sound like a convoluted way to say “ice,” but experts would disagree. In any case, it is at least soft enough to be poured into and out of a bottle.

32970.description:
Though widely disparaged as fool's gold, there are certain obsessive miners who would trade sacks of genuine precious metal for this glorious hunk of iron and sulphur.

※For collectable submissions only.

32971.description:
“If you can't recognize the beauty inherent in its orthorhombic crystal system, then we can't be friends.”

※For collectable submissions only.

32972.description:
Artistic collectors will swoon over the lustrous ochre pigment that can be produced from this seemingly unremarkable rock of iron ore.

※For collectable submissions only.

32973.description:
Vanu shamans collect spring water to make the paste they apply to their beaks before rituals. Some Vanu shamans are very, *very* particular about their spring water.

※For collectable submissions only.

32974.description:
When the aether of one's opus must *flow* unimpeded, one cannot skimp on the conductive component of one's ink.

※For collectable submissions only.

32975.description:
The potential value of this uncut stone is obvious to the practiced eye. Especially if you love yellow.

※For collectable submissions only.

32976.description:
Rubies are red. Sapphires are blue. Star spinels are more of a violet, though, and that's the hue glinting from within this promising stone.

※For collectable submissions only.

32977.description:
“If I can cut this just so, it will provide the perfect accent for a rather rakish turban I've been weaving...”

※For collectable submissions only.

32978.description:
Be sure to don your swimming trunks before losing yourself in the deep, deep blue of this entrancing raw gemstone.

※For collectable submissions only.

32979.description:
“It's beautiful! Stunning! Magnificent! Now find me three more.”

※For collectable submissions only.

32980.description:
Never has titanium and copper existed in a more harmonious blend of minerals. It promises to make a wonderful teapot.

※For collectable submissions only.

32981.description:
One day, this unfinished gemstone of clearest blue could grace an elegant ring or an exquisite necklace or a face-smashing fist weapon. Possibilities!

※For collectable submissions only.

32982.description:
Not quite clear and not quite white, you're not quite sure why the jewel hiding in this rock is so valuable.

※For collectable submissions only.

32983.description:
“Don't you *dare* throw that over your shoulder. Here, use the table salt.”

※For collectable submissions only.

32984.description:
They say reef rock has been procured for restoration projects in a certain snowbound city. Perhaps this perfectly porous piece is destined for a structure of “holey” importance.

※For collectable submissions only.

32985.description:
Even in its rough, natural form, the shimmering blackness of this jewel is almost dangerously captivating. So...pretty...

※For collectable submissions only.

32986.description:
A truly precious find for one invested in the finest facets of tungsten-based fabrication.

※For collectable submissions only.

32987.description:
“Well, tan my hide! You must have spent *weeks* in the mountains of Eastern Aldenard looking for this stuff.” 

※For collectable submissions only.

32988.description:
Unconfirmed rumors tell of an eccentric Lalafell with plans to use these glowing grains to build a private beach. She'll probably need a few more handfuls...

※For collectable submissions only.

32989.description:
Should probably be saved for the concoction of valuable reisui, but it *does* make for a tasty cup of buckwheat tea.

※For collectable submissions only.

32990.description:
If this mineral was any aether-richer, it would have to pay taxes.

※For collectable submissions only.

32991.description:
The customer requesting this liquid-like sand was oddly specific about the number of grains in the handful.

※For collectable submissions only.

32992.description:
Rather than experiment with amusing applications for this superior sticky substance, it's perhaps best to relinquish it to a tree sap professional.

※For collectable submissions only.

32993.description:
Gazing upon this rough-cut log, you cannot help but wonder if its lustrous lumber is destined for a valiant knight's lance or a bilge-bottomed buccaneer's bar stool. Anyone's guess, really.

※For collectable submissions only.

32994.description:
“Aye, 'twould make a fine sentinel's longbow. But see, I have this prior commission to craft a fishing rod. N-No, that's not my penmanship!”

※For collectable submissions only.

32995.description:
A champion among chestnuts, predestined for the summit of a Sohm Al tart.

※For collectable submissions only.

32996.description:
The viscous lifeblood you extracted from a vigorous yet defenseless chestnut tree. You monster.

※For collectable submissions only.

32997.description:
You wonder if the fact that “larch log” is fun to say has anything to do with its inherent collectability.

※For collectable submissions only.

32998.description:
Only the finest fungi are foraged for fancy Far Eastern feast tables.

※For collectable submissions only.

32999.description:
Larch...sap. No, not nearly so fun to say as “larch log” but apparently just as collectable.

※For collectable submissions only.

33000.description:
Unsurprisingly, this exceptionally gooey mass is a prime ingredient in certain beetle-based adhesives.

※For collectable submissions only.

33001.description:
Almost unnaturally straight and true, this log will hopefully be processed into lumber for a future masterpiece of carpentry...and not thrown into some chilly lordling's fireplace.

※For collectable submissions only.

33002.description:
One bite of this almost unbearably sweet fruit will have you flitting about like a pollen-drunk pixie.

※For collectable submissions only.

33003.description:
A difficult material to work with, any artisan would nevertheless be eager to craft an enduring handle or lasting piece of furniture from this marvelous hunk of hardwood.

※For collectable submissions only.

33004.description:
The real miracle here is that any of these trees were left standing after a sudden and inexplicable surge in the demand for applewood staves.

※For collectable submissions only.

33005.description:
After being carved and then covered with exquisitely woven wool, this attractive lump of timber could serve as the elegant display stand for some staggeringly expensive─and rarely worn─neckwear.

※For collectable submissions only.

33006.description:
“Yes, an oriental breakfast is generally a simple affair, but that doesn't mean one should settle for any old seaweed in the sea.”

※For collectable submissions only.

33007.description:
Once dried and enshrined in a sturdy jar, these flavorsome flower buds will take pride of place on a master chef's spice shelf.

※For collectable submissions only.

33008.description:
“This is it! The perfect piece of coral to complement my perfect coral butterfly. My aquarium is complete!”

※For collectable submissions only.

33009.description:
Compared to your average cut of timber, the quality of this log is the difference between urunight and urunday.

※For collectable submissions only.

33010.description:
Is it gold? Is it blue? Or mayhap green? Folk will spend all day arguing over the color of a dress made from these prismatic cotton fibers.

※For collectable submissions only.

33011.description:
Either this is the bloodiest bloodhemp you've ever harvested, or some small vermin with terrible situational awareness came between the plant and your scythe.

※For collectable submissions only.

33012.description:
This incredibly hardy plant specimen is able to thrive under almost any conditions...except one populated by single-minded botanists.

※For collectable submissions only.

33013.description:
Guaranteed to make you sneeze. Just...aim it away from the cooking pot.

※For collectable submissions only.

33147.description: A carefully prepared blend of soil and decaying leaves.

33148.description: An aromatic herb used in various dishes and remedies.

33149.description: A versatile herb that grows easily in moist soil.

33150.description: A fragrant herb popular with culinarians...and their customers.

33151.description: Once consumed exclusively by the upper classes but now available to the hoi polloi.

33152.description: A solid piece of cooled lava, its burning fury in a dormant state.

33229.description: Cleanliness being paramount, the infirmary can never have too many items such as soap─nor the materials with which they are made.

33230.description: Being a medical facility, Ser Vaindreau's Grace ever has need of─you guessed it─medical supplies, and these materials are suitable for crafting them.

33231.description: These strong and sturdy materials should make strong and sturdy rehabilitation aids for the patients of Ser Vaindreau's Grace.

33232.description: No high tea is complete without scrumptious sweets, and the ingredients needed in their creation, such as syrups, never go astray.

33233.description: If art is like salve for the soul, then these materials are the ingredients for said salve.

35600.description: A must-have for anyone looking to recreate Hannish culture.

35601.description: A must-have for anyone looking to recreate Garlean culture.

35602.description: A must-have for anyone looking to recreate lunar culture.

35603.description: A must-have for anyone looking to recreate the culture of Elpis.

35847.description: Can be used to craft a beautiful hairpin in the right hands.

35848.description: Can be used to craft a beautiful ring in the right hands.

36083.description: A superlative grain cultivated over time to withstand disease and produce greater harvests.

36084.description: A bluish grey salt extracted from the islands of the northern seas.

36085.description: An annual herb, grown on the island of Thavnair and known for its superb medicinal properties.

36086.description: A sweet sap extracted from the same trees that produce coconuts.

36087.description: In the southern seas, Lalafells will launch their brave comrades from catapults in order to fetch these palm seedlings from tall trees.

36088.description: A leafy, moisture-rich vegetable cultivated in Labyrinthos.

36089.description: An alarmingly overgrown popoto suitable for raising hearty Lalafells. (Any Lalafells reading this may rest assured that this does not qualify as cannibalism.)

36090.description: A nutrient-rich vegetable beloved by Loporrits. Just one nibble is enough to inspire feelings of euphoria.

36091.description: Garleans will often pickle this vine-grown fruit and then drink the juice as a hangover cure.

36092.description: Legumes that grow well in cold climates.

36093.description: A Garlean root vegetable that boasts a deep red color from its stem to its bulb.

36094.description: The tea produced from this plant is somewhat bitter but possesses incredible medicinal properties.

36095.description: An ancient spice that emits a sweet aroma. Used in cooking as well as in medicine.

36096.description: A fruit known as a symbol of vitality and the lushness of nature.

36097.description: A bizarre bulb that isn't actually an onion but looks vaguely reminiscent of one...

36098.description: A brightly colored pepper produced on the island of Thavnair.

36162.description: Sand consisting of tiny grains of high durium.

36174.description: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be ametrine.

36177.description: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be blue zircon.

36178.description: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be star quartz.

36179.description: Sand consisting of tiny grains of rhodium.

36180.description: A crystalline schist formed in low temperatures and under little pressure.

36181.description: A decent-sized chunk of rock made up of what appears to be thousands of thin sheets of dark grey crystal compacted together into a single mass.

36190.description: A rough-cut log of horse chestnut timber.

36191.description: A rough-cut log of palm timber.

36192.description: A rough-cut log of red pine timber.

36193.description: A rough-cut log of ironwood timber.

36194.description: A rough-cut log of an unknown composite wood.

36195.description: A rough-cut log of mempisang timber.

36202.description: Native to the islands of the north seas, the fibrous stem of this plant can be used to weave cloth.

36204.description: Sourced from the northern reaches of Ilsabard.

36205.description: An ancient species of moko grass which can be used to weave cloth.

36206.description: A rare variety of cotton which has been beloved as long as you can remember...which is not very long, given that your mind goes blank each time you attempt to recall its origins.

36207.description: These shining cocoons are woven only by Thavnairian silkworms.

36214.description: Not for the weak of heart or palate, this powdered mixture of natural spices gives any dish a flavorsome kick.

36215.description: Water so replete with minerals that drinking it unboiled is inadvisable, regardless of how appealing that may seem.

36216.description: This sample displays the particular dolomitization characteristic of the frozen wilds of Ilsabard.

36217.description: Incredibly potent, but also incredibly hard to find without getting lost in the woods and meeting an untimely end.

36241.description: An alumen sourced from the Eblan Rime.

36263.description: Such fresh rainwater can only be collected on the highest of high isles in the sky.

36285.description: A grey rock tinged with a ghostly green hue.

36286.description: A rock with an elemental aspect leaning unnaturally towards umbral.

36287.description: Clay said to have been used to craft Thaliak's very own ewer.

36288.description: Bark from a Thavnairian palm tree.

36291.description:
Donning equipment crafted from this elegant emerald alloy is sure to turn onlookers green with envy...right?

※For collectable submissions only.

36292.description:
Some say peering into the murky depths of this stone will reveal secret truths of existence─for instance, that staring at a rock for extended periods causes significant ocular discomfort.

※For collectable submissions only.

36293.description:
This multicolored beauty was born from the fusion of amethyst and citrine.

※For collectable submissions only.

36294.description:
This mineral may look like a shiny rock, but when oxidized, it becomes a *very* shiny rock.

※For collectable submissions only.

36295.description:
“Everyone talks so much about how salt *tastes* and not enough about how it *looks*.”

※For collectable submissions only.

36296.description:
Not everything that glitters is gold─sometimes it is much more valuable.

※For collectable submissions only.

36297.description:
The brilliance of this sample's blue hue remains nigh unparalleled in the natural world─particularly now that it has been removed from it.

※For collectable submissions only.

36298.description:
No one would call this alumen “rarefied” were it overabundant in the frozen north─certainly not for marketing purposes. Perish the thought!

※For collectable submissions only.

36299.description:
Handling may cause this mineral to fracture or flake, so best not. What do you mean, “too late”?

※For collectable submissions only.

36300.description:
Pewter? I barely know her!

※For collectable submissions only.

36301.description:
This herb's minty aroma is stronger than that of its perilla brethren, easily separating the Thavs from the Thav-nots.

※For collectable submissions only.

36302.description:
More wood than iron...which is to say that it is not really iron at all.

※For collectable submissions only.

36303.description:
The lack of rings makes this lumber impossible to date─or, as particularly aggravating naturalists might say, “stuck in the frond zone.”

※For collectable submissions only.

36304.description:
While this wood is more red-adjacent than truly red, “red-adjacent pine” does not exactly roll off the tongue.

※For collectable submissions only.

36305.description:
Though this deceptive drupe does not taste like cocoa and it is not a true nut, culinarians tend to overlook these offenses in light of its deliciousness. It is on thin ice with the botanists, however.

※For collectable submissions only.

36306.description:
A succulent symbol of vitality, this fruit pairs nicely with some honey and stone cheese.

※For collectable submissions only.

36307.description:
This hearty grain is a culinarian's delight─though much more so after the tiresome grinding step is complete.

※For collectable submissions only.

36308.description:
This sweet-scented spice is proven to help medicine go down. Consuming an entire spoonful, however, is not recommended.

※For collectable submissions only.

36309.description:
This crisp, refreshing vegetable is often thought to be lacking in flavor, but those who enjoy the flavor of water doubtless find it absolutely overpowering.

※For collectable submissions only.

36310.description:
These bolls are so irresistibly soft that some folks can't help but pluck them and pop them in their ears. Caution: under no circumstances should AR-Caean cotton be placed near the ears.

※For collectable submissions only.

36669.description: This aetheroconductive feather is destined to become the much-needed quill of a student lacking one.

36670.description: A sack of rare materials essential in the crafting of aetheroconductive foci.

36671.description: This may be the most extravagant set of materials you have ever seen used to craft what is essentially a box for one's lunch.

36672.description: These aetheroconductive materials will make for highly responsive mammets, perfect for any aspiring mage's needs.

36673.description: These materials can be used to craft school supplies─and hopefully a brighter future for the children in need of them.

37278.description: A selectively bred variant cultivated from the maize once brought to Thavnair from the New World. Valued for its nutritional value and alchemical uses alike.

37279.description: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be Eblan danburite.

37691.description: This sap-coated plant has taken on a glossy, crystalline appearance, but it is yet in flux. Under the right conditions, it could become sublime.

37694.description: A ferrous meteorite in apparent flux. Under the right conditions, it could become sublime.

37817.description: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be rutilated quartz.

37818.description: A rough-cut log of paldao timber.

37819.description: A Thavnairian nut often used in dyeing and tanning practices.

37820.description: A hunk of moon ore rich in titanium.

37821.description: A small branch of wax myrtle clipped from a shrub in Labyrinthos.

37822.description: Soil rich in diatoms and cultivated in Labyrinthos to superior quality.

38788.description: A material harvested with the discerning standards of an avid collector in mind. This semi-fossilized bark is guaranteed to survive being forgotten for several decades in the back of a reagent drawer.

38790.description: A mineral excavated with the discerning standards of an avid collector in mind. All the colors of the rainbow dance within this mesmerizing rock.

38794.description: A material harvested with the discerning standards of an avid collector in mind. Even the aroma from this mint is enough to set one's tongue to tingling.

38796.description: A mineral excavated with the discerning standards of an avid collector in mind. Once ground, this gemstone should provide a striking crimson pigment for use in dyes.

38821.description: This bundle of flammable material is one spark away from a roaring fire─for better or worse.

38822.description: The precise nature of these ingredients is unknown, but their addition to Voeburtite cuisine has undeniably delicious results.

38823.description: Material ideal for the construction of Voeburtite handicrafts, including (but not limited to) sheep paraphernalia.

38824.description: An offering of whimsical miscellanea coveted by any pixie.

38933.description: The quality of this bark is undeniable and likely due to the hospitable surrounds of Labyrinthos.

38934.description: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be zoisite.

38937.description: A rock with an elemental aspect leaning heavily towards earth.

38938.description: Tendrils of a perennial plant replete with earth aether.

39234.description: A spongy mushroom imbued with fascinating life energy. Under the right conditions, it could become sublime.

39237.description: A meteorite primarily comprised of olivine and pyroxene. Under the right conditions, it could become sublime.

39705.description: A rough-cut log of dark cherry timber.

39706.description: A decent-sized piece of rock containing a naturally occurring mix of silver and quicksilver.

39707.description: An uncut, unpolished stone containing what appears to be spodumene.

39708.description: Originating in Thavnair, this iron oxide is often utilized as a pigment for its rusty red hue.

39709.description: The oil extracted from the seeds of this vivid yellow flower has various practical applications, not the least of which is as a reagent for curing skins and hides.

39710.description: A prize “flower” grown in the nightmare fungal garden of Lovingway's Darlings.

39805.description: A material harvested with the discerning standards of an avid collector in mind, and well suited to aetherial reduction. Whether the layer of filth is truly required for it to maintain this property remains unclear, but why take the risk?

39807.description: A fruit harvested with the discerning standards of an avid collector in mind, and well suited to aetherial reduction (or consumption by hungry artisans).

39811.description: A mineral harvested with the discerning standards of an avid collector in mind, and royally suited to aetherial reduction.

39813.description: A material harvested with the discerning standards of an avid collector in mind, and well suited to aetherial reduction. Also, pies.

39906.description: A lustrous leaf of the plant born from the popular Thavnairian nut. Under the right conditions, it could become sublime.
